headline: Houthi strikes cripple Saudi oil, Yemen launches offensive, escalating Middle East conflict
subheadline: Omani pilot tried to crash a plane at Ben Gurion, stopped by a pilot, as Houthis fire Khurais oil facility and East-West pipeline in Riyadh
lede: Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered an audit of foreign aviation security after an Omani pilot plotted to crash a plane at Ben Gurion Airport and a Dubai flight hijacking attempt occurred. Houthi forces launched coordinated attacks on Saudi Aramco’s Khurais oil facility and the East-West pipeline, igniting widespread fires in Riyadh, prompting Yemen to declare a military offensive to retake territory from the Houthis. In Ukraine, Russian forces are fighting for four settlements—Varvarovka, Nikolaevka, Lobanovka, and Reznikov—in a Kharkiv encirclement while a massive drone wave of jet‑powered Shaheds penetrates northern and central regions, prompting Kyiv to deploy AI‑controlled turrets and Zelensky to unveil a new ballistic missile reaching Moscow. Germany delivered €1.3 billion in military aid, including anti‑jet drone production and AI‑guided turrets now being installed around the capital, as the U.S. proposes trilateral talks by month’s end.

sections.title: Middle East Escalation: Aviation Audit and Houthi Strikes
sections.body: Prime Minister Netanyahu instructed the Civil Service head to appoint an auditor to examine foreign aviation security following a series of failures, including an Omani pilot’s plot to crash a plane at Ben Gurion Airport and a Dubai flight hijacking attempt. Houthi forces attacked Saudi Aramco’s Khurais oil processing facility and the East-West pipeline, causing widespread fires in Riyadh. The Yemeni government announced a military operation to retake territory from the Houthis, marking a major escalation in the regional proxy conflict. The IDF eliminated Hamas terrorist Nabil Musa Qaisi, involved in the October 7 massacre, in Khan Younis, while Iran summoned Norway’s ambassador to protest Oslo’s failure to block unauthorized Starlink operations.

sections.title: Ukraine Counteroffensive: Drone Wave and German Aid
sections.body: Russian forces are engaged in combat for four settlements—Varvarovka, Nikolaevka, Lobanovka, and Reznikov—within a Kharkiv region encirclement, according to the Russian Ministry of Defense. Ukraine is experiencing a significant drone wave with jet‑powered Shaheds and high‑speed targets penetrating northern and central regions, including Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy, and Kharkiv. Germany provided €1.3 billion in military aid, encompassing joint anti‑jet drone production, long‑range weapons, combat drones, and satellites, while Kyiv installed AI‑controlled machine gun turrets against jet Shaheds, with 12+ already deployed. President Zelensky announced intensified retaliation against Russian oil infrastructure, unveiled a new ballistic missile reaching Moscow, and noted Russia holds 700 ballistic missiles with 140 produced monthly, as the U.S. proposes trilateral talks by end‑October.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The simultaneous Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Yemen’s counter‑offensive signal a deepening proxy war escalation, while Israel’s aviation security audit underscores internal vulnerabilities exposed by the Omani pilot plot. In Ukraine, Russia’s coordinated ground encirclement and massive drone campaign, coupled with a sustained ballistic missile inventory, indicate a high‑intensity air war, countered by Ukraine’s AI turrets and new long‑range strike capability, with diplomatic uncertainty introduced by the proposed U.S. trilateral talks.
